proposed.name: Compatible response laws
proposed.construction:
\[
\mathcal Q_T(p)=\left\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal R_T):
\begin{array}{ll}
\Pr_q(X_z=x,V_x=y)=p^z_{xy},
  &x\in T,\\
\Pr_q(X_z=x,W_{xz}=y)=p^z_{xy},
  &x\in U,
\end{array}
\quad z,y\in\{0,1\}\right\}.
\]
This is the saturated individual-level selected-exclusion response model on \(\mathcal R_T\).  For every trusted category \(x\in T\), the single binary variable \(V_x\) is an arm-invariant potential outcome and is used in the compatibility equation for both instrument arms.  For every untrusted category \(x\in U\), the two binary coordinates \(W_{x0}\) and \(W_{x1}\) are arm-specific labels used only to complete the factual outcome on the events \(\{X_0=x\}\) and \(\{X_1=x\}\), respectively.  They are not asserted to be outcomes under an intervention setting exposure to \(x\), and no cross-arm equality is imposed on them.  When \(T=\mathcal E\), the untrusted block is empty; the statement that this full-trust specialization is Song--Guo--Chan--Richardson model \(\mathcal M_1\) means equality of the response image in the joint law of \(V\) and the observed table \(p\), as established in \(\mathrm{prop{:}published\mbox{-}reductions}\).  When \(T=\{a,b\}\) and the nonempty set \(U\) is aggregated to one remainder label, the Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander comparison means equality of the sharp \(\theta_{ab}\)-projection and its eight affine endpoint formulas; it does not assert identity between the latent fine-exposure model classes.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement makes the saturated selected-exclusion semantics explicit: trusted coordinates are shared potential outcomes, whereas untrusted coordinates are arm-specific factual completion labels. It also records the exact image/projection scope of the Song and Gabriel comparisons without changing the model equations, assumptions, or endpoint formula.

prose_updates.tldr: With a randomized binary instrument, binary outcome, and arbitrary finite categorical exposure, the maintained model is a saturated individual-level selected-exclusion response model. Trusted categories have shared arm-invariant potential outcomes, while untrusted categories have only arm-specific labels that complete factual outcomes and are not treated as interventions. The sharp pairwise-effect interval is governed by one two-diagonal capacity: each endpoint evaluates eight baseline affine pieces and exactly two pieces per trusted nuisance category, with finite laws attaining both endpoints. Trust is nested by an explicit response-law restriction map, and separate positive-cell witnesses show strict observed-law enlargement from selected trust and strict identified-set tightening from adding trust. Comparator scope is exact: Balke--Pearl is recovered literally only for a binary exposure; aggregating a wholly untrusted remainder recovers the relevant Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander sharp projection and formula, not an identity of latent fine-exposure model classes; and arbitrary finite full trust has the Song--Guo--Chan--Richardson model M1 response image, with the pairwise interval transferring to models M2 through M5 by their equal-image theorem. Finite-sample whole-set coverage remains valid at ties and zero cells.

project_justification.gap: Balke and Pearl give the literal binary-exposure envelope. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjolander give the sharp target projection for two well-defining target levels with one merged potentially ill-defining remainder, as well as the ten-term fully trusted ternary formulas; those results do not identify a latent fine-exposure class with an arbitrary refinement of the remainder. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson characterize arbitrary finite categorical exposure under full trust and prove that five IV formulations have the same joint potential-outcome and observed-law image, but leave scalar pairwise endpoints to generic optimization. What is missing is an arbitrary-finite sharp scalar envelope for the saturated selected-exclusion model in which only declared categories possess shared potential outcomes, together with an exact nesting map and strict witnesses on the common observed-law domain.
project_justification.niche: Applied adherence studies often have two interventionally meaningful target categories, several intermediate categories for which exclusion may be separately defensible, and residual categories for which no cross-instrument outcome equality is credible. The residual-category variables needed to represent factual outcomes should not thereby be promoted to potential outcomes under ill-defined interventions. This structure is neither a binary exposure model nor a fully exclusion-valid categorical model.
project_justification.fill: The paper formalizes the saturated selected-exclusion response law by separating shared potential outcomes on trusted categories from arm-specific factual completion labels on untrusted categories. Its two-diagonal transport reduction supplies the sharp linear-size envelope and finite endpoint laws. The response-law restriction map proves that enlarging trust nests both compatibility classes and identified sets; the separation and gain tables make both inclusions strict in the appropriate sense. Exact reductions recover Balke--Pearl only on a genuinely binary alphabet, recover Gabriel's merged-remainder and ternary sharp projections and formulas in their stated scopes without equating latent fine-exposure classes, and identify the arbitrary-finite full-trust response image with Song's M1 image before transferring the target projection to Song's other four equal-image models.

prose_updates.related_work: Balke and Pearl derive eight sharp affine average-effect expressions for binary instrument, binary exposure, and binary outcome; the present formula is called literally Balke--Pearl only when the exposure alphabet has two elements. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjolander Result 1 treats two well-defining target exposure levels plus one merged potentially ill-defining remainder and recovers those eight expressions, while their equations (3)--(4) give ten sharp expressions per endpoint for three well-defining exposure levels. The selected-trust comparison with their Result 1 is equality of the relevant sharp target projection and endpoint formula after aggregation; it is not an identity between their three-label latent model and this paper's arbitrary fine-exposure latent class. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjolander, and Gabriel provide general symbolic primal--dual machinery for finite response-function models; that machinery informs certification but is not the linear-size envelope proved here. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson characterize arbitrary categorical IV models under full trust. Precisely, when every category is trusted, this paper's saturated response model has the same image in the joint potential-outcome law and observed table as their model M1. Their Theorem 1 gives equality of that joint-potential-outcome/observed-law image across models M1 through M5, so taking the pairwise-effect projection transfers the sharp interval to all five formulations. This image statement is not imposed on selected-trust laws, whose untrusted arm-specific labels are factual completion variables rather than intervention outcomes. Bhadane, Mooij, Boeken, and Zoeter Theorem 17 gives the observed full-exclusion compatibility characterization for binary instrument and outcome with arbitrary finite exposure. The cell-sum inequality violated by the separation family is attributed to that observed-model result and also follows directly because the two relevant full-exclusion factual events are disjoint. That family is selected-trust compatible on a positive-cell neighborhood but not full-trust representable, whereas the separate full-trust-compatible gain table shows strict identified-set tightening after trusting the intermediate category. VanderWeele and Hernan explain why coarse labels may hide treatment versions, and Marshall studies bias from coarsening; they motivate the distinction between a trusted refinement and a wholly untrusted split or merge. Zhang, Frazier, Poskitt, and Zhao analyze identification gains for binary average-effect bounds; the categorywise active-face update here is a corollary of the sharp envelope. Du Toit and collaborators supply the LEAP adherence application in which separately justified intermediate consumption categories may or may not change the low-versus-high interval.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The untrusted variables in the saturated response space are arm-specific factual completion labels only; no result interprets them as potential outcomes under category interventions. The count of eight plus twice the number of trusted nuisance categories denotes a complete affine evaluation list for each endpoint, not an assertion that every listed term is an irredundant facet on every lower-dimensional support stratum. A wholly untrusted refinement preserves both endpoints: push a factual coupling forward through the refinement map, and lift it by arbitrary disintegration within each untrusted fiber. Compute the eight baseline faces, scan the trusted nuisance categories, update the lower maximum and upper minimum with the two category faces, and retain ties; this uses linear arithmetic in the alphabet size and constant auxiliary memory beyond the input and active-face output. These are formula and implementation consequences, not independent research targets. Producing a full attaining transport by generic augmenting paths is claimed only to terminate in finite polynomial time.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The sole identification kernel is the sharp-envelope theorem for the saturated selected-exclusion response model, with its transport completion and finite endpoint-attaining laws. Shared potential outcomes exist only for trusted categories; untrusted response coordinates are factual completion labels with no intervention interpretation. The perturbation-stable non-representability family and the separate open strict-gain region provide the load-bearing comparison with full exclusion. At full trust, the comparison with Song et al. is equality of the joint-potential-outcome/observed-law response image; after merging a wholly untrusted remainder, the Gabriel comparison is equality of the relevant sharp projection and formula, not an identity of latent fine-exposure classes. The Hoeffding whole-set theorem supplies finite-sample coverage. The categorywise trust update is a one-line corollary, wholly untrusted refinement is a formula remark, and one-pass evaluation is an implementation note. The bounded computations are diagnostic evidence rather than theorem premises. The Outlook question remains open over triangular arrays without cell, face-gap, or face-variance floors, while its strict precision comparison is restricted to nonempty compact regular classes. No monotonicity, exposure ordering, instrument relevance, exposure-cell positivity, or clinical justification of any trusted LEAP category is claimed.
